narrative.overview:
Every slide is a flight-progress strip racked in deck order on a gray-green console, and the presenter works the deck the way a controller works traffic. Paper strips sit in colored plastic holders. Printed fields are divided by hairline rules. A lamp lights when Copilot is working a strip, and a pen mark settles it. The interface is dense, calm and operational; it rewards scanning a long rack, not admiring a hero.

Hierarchy comes from scale and position rather than color: the strip in hand is lifted out of the rack at display scale, flanked by its neighbors, above a registered comparison of current and proposed notes. Most slides are already fine, so the rack stays quiet. Color appears only where a slide needs something or where work is happening.

The system rejects the card-grid dashboard with a stats header. Slides are never tiles; they are strips in deck order.
keyCharacteristics: A gray-green console bay ground with a dark green-graphite rail across the top.
Warm paper strips in amber, steel or graphite holders, segmented into printed fields with 1px rules.
B612 for words, B612 Mono for everything counted, numbered or printed as a field.
One cyan lamp for the Copilot loop; hand-drawn pen marks for accepted and rejected.
Tight corners (2–5px), physical rack depth, no pills and no gradients on surfaces.

rules.name: The Holder Is a Fact Rule
rules.body: Holder color encodes the slide as uploaded (needs notes, OK, skip) and never changes with workflow. Workflow state lives in the lamp, the state label and the pen mark.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Lamp cyan is reserved for the Copilot loop (in research, to review, cocked) and for focus. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Paper Not White Rule
rules.body: Reading surfaces are warm paper. Pure white is only the momentary lift of a hovered or active strip or key.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Words in B612; numbers, counts, field names and log lines in B612 Mono with tabular numerals. Never set a count in the sans.

rules.name: The Scale Contrast Rule
rules.body: The lifted title sits at display scale against 10px mono field labels. Hierarchy comes from that contrast, not from extra weights or colored headings.

rules.name: The Printed Field Rule
rules.body: Uppercase mono labels name the data in a printed field or divide the rack into sections. They never sit above a headline as a kicker.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: Strip columns are sized to their longest label: designator 4rem, notes 5.75rem, flags 2.75rem, state 6.75rem. The title is the only column that ellipsizes; on narrow racks a field is dropped, never truncated.

rules.name: The Rack Depth Rule
rules.body: Elevation means where a strip is in the rack (racked, cocked, lifted), never decoration or hover. Keys get only a 1px underline shadow and press down 1px.

dos: **Do** set every number, count and field value in B612 Mono with tabular numerals.
**Do** show notes health on the five-tick ramp (1/40/80/120/160 words) next to the count.
**Do** mark accepted strips with the cleared-green pen check and rejected ones with the vermilion pen strike.
**Do** set current and proposed notes at the same measure (68ch) and line height (1.65) so the comparison is registered.
**Do** cock a strip 14px out of the rack when its proposal arrives, and keep it cocked until it is opened.
donts: **Don't** lay slides out as a card grid or open a view with a stats header; slides are strips in deck order.
**Don't** use holder color to signal workflow state; holders are facts about the uploaded slide.
**Don't** use lamp cyan for anything outside the Copilot loop and focus.
**Don't** put uppercase mono labels above headings as kickers; they name printed fields only.
**Don't** let a fixed strip field truncate; size the column to its longest label or drop the field at a container breakpoint.
**Don't** round corners beyond 6px or use pill shapes.
